definitions.explanation: Describes food or drink that tastes good. One of the most common and useful adjectives for expressing positive opinions about food. Used in everyday conversation.
Colloquially used to describe a situation that is favorable or beneficial.

examples.japanese: ⟦これ→これ：00963_kore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{美味|おい}しい⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
{美味|おい}しい⟦レストラン→れすとらん：01048_resutoran⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}っています→しる：00458_shiru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Do you know a good restaurant?
examples.notes: 美味しい here means 'good' for food

examples.japanese: ⟦お{母|かあ}さん→おかあさん：02851_okaasan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{魚|さかな}→さかな：00499_sakana⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧{美味|おい}しい⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
⟦{友達|ともだち}→ともだち：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{作|つく}った→つくる：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→りょうり：01523_ryouri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧{美味|おい}しくて、⟦びっくりしました→びっくり：03003_bikkuri⟧。
examples.english: The food my friend made was so delicious that I was surprised.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{店|みせ}→みせ：00497_mise⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{魚|さかな}→さかな：00499_sakana⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{新鮮|しんせん}→しんせん：03261_shinsen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{美味|おい}しい⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。⟦{毎週|まいしゅう}→まいしゅう：00730_maishuu⟧⟦{来|き}たくなる→くる：00254_kuru⟧⟦ほど→ほど：01724_hodo⟧⟦{気|き}に{入|い}っています→きにいる：02047_kiniiru⟧。
examples.english: The fish at this restaurant is fresh and delicious. I like it so much that I want to come every week.

examples.japanese: それは{美味|おい}しい{話|はなし}だね。
examples.english: That sounds like a sweet deal.

notes:
{美味|おい}しい is an i-adjective. While the kanji form exists, the word is more commonly written in hiragana as おいしい.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: おいしく ({美味|おい}しく{作|つく}る — to make deliciously)
- Negative: おいしくない (not delicious)
- Past: おいしかった (was delicious)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦うまい→うまい：01279_umai⟧: also means delicious, but more casual/masculine
- ⟦{不味|まず}い→まずい：00733_mazui⟧: bad-tasting (opposite)

SENSE 2 (COLLOQUIAL):
{美味|おい}しい{話|はなし} means "a sweet deal" or "too-good-to-be-true offer." This figurative use is common in casual conversation.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Saying おいしい while eating is a natural and polite way to compliment the cook. It is one of the first words learners should know for dining situations.
